title: Chief Operations Officer at State Bank of India Sees Digital-Sovereignty Spending Rising as Localization Requirements Expand
expert: Former Chief Operations Officer at State Bank of India (530M+ customers); saw technology procurement and cloud partnerships including AWS
verdict: SBI's IT and digital-sovereignty spend rises from $1–$2 billion in FY2026 to $2–$3 billion in FY2027, with AWS one of four clouds and the provider for Mumbai and Hyderabad.

AWS growth: 🟢 SBI IT spend \$1–\$2 billion to \$2–\$3 billion (FY2026 to FY2027 plan), cloud and data engineering +15%–20% a year (estimate); fits Jassy's 2026 capacity fully committed (SB #62035). → Thesis ('Huge AI winner') ↑
🟡 AWS one of four clouds (Mumbai and Hyderabad; Azure in South India) and Tier 1–3 banking workloads must stay in-country; first read. → Thesis (AWS growth) →
AWS margins: 🟡 80% of budget goes direct to OEMs, 20% to integrators, while the bank targets a 20%–30% lower operating-cost model; first read. → Thesis (AWS margins) →

changes: Demand: SBI cloud and data engineering +15%–20% in FY2027 vs Jassy (2026-10-27): 2026 capacity fully committed, 2027 largely sold out (SB #62035): consistent.
First read on an Indian bank's cloud and sovereignty budget; the 2026-11-05 AMZN calls covered marketplace and India affiliates, not cloud spend.
thesis_impact: Thesis ('Huge AI winner', 20% AWS growth bogey): ↑ — a large AWS customer plans IT spend of \$2–\$3 billion in FY2027 from \$1–\$2 billion, cloud +15%–20%.
Thesis (AWS margins): → — multi-cloud by design (AWS, Google, Azure, Oracle) and a 20%–30% lower operating-cost target limit pricing leverage.
